p.docTitle: Adopted by the Security Council at its 10241st meeting, on14 October 2026

container.name: Reaffirming
container.p: Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of Haiti,

container.name: Recalling
container.p: Recalling its previous resolutions on Haiti, in particular its resolutions 2653 (2022), 2700 (2023), 2752 (2024), 2793 (2025), 2794 (2025), and 2829 (2026),

container.name: Expressing
container.p: Expressing grave concern about the extremely high levels of gang violence and other criminal activities in Haiti, including kidnappings, trafficking in persons, migrant smuggling, homicides, and sexual violence, including rape and sexual slavery as well as the killing, maiming, abduction, sexual violence and the recruitment of children by gangs, as well as ongoing impunity for perpetrators, enablers, and financiers,

container.name: Expressing grave
container.p: Expressing grave concern that illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition to armed gangs in Haiti continues to fuel this violence, undermine the rule of law and respect for human rights, and can impede the provision of humanitarian assistance, which can have wide-ranging negative humanitarian, socioeconomic, and regional consequences, and urging Member States to take urgent and decisive measures to fully implement the arms embargo,

container.name: Encouraging
container.p: Encouraging Member States to support the Commission Nationale de Désarmement, Démantèlement et de Réinsertion (National Commission for Disarmament, Dismantlement and Reintegration (CNDDR’s) 2026 Intervention Strategy, including through support for the UN Haiti Peace Dividends Fund, and to build Haitian National Police (HNP) and Armed Forces of Haiti Forces’ (FAd’H) capacities,

container.name: Recognizing
container.p: Recognizing the need to safeguard due process, and to ensure fair and clear procedures for delisting individuals and entities designated pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022) and subsequent resolutions, and welcoming the appointment of the Focal Point for Delisting, while further recognizing the role of UN sanctions in conflict resolution and maintaining international peace and security,

container.name: Determining
container.p: Determining that the situation in Haiti continues to constitute a threat to international peace and security in the region,

container.name: Acting
container.p: Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

paragraph.subheading: Travel Ban, Asset Freeze, and Arms Embargo

content.p: Decides to renew until one year from the date of adoption of this resolution the measures imposed by paragraphs 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 of resolution 2653 (2022) and previously extended in resolution 2794 (2025), reaffirms resolution 2664 (2022) and affirms that paragraphs 15 and 16 of resolution 2653 (2022) shall continue to apply and decides that actions as described in paragraph 15 of resolution 2653 (2022) include engaging in activities that destabilize Haiti through the illicit exploitation or trade of natural resources; further encourages the Haitian authorities to adopt a decree regulating the exploitation of elvers and related trade; and further decides to extend the measures imposed by paragraph 2 of resolution 2794 (2025) for one year from the date of adoption of this resolution;

Expresses concern at reports of misappropriation, embezzlement and diversion of public resources which pose a risk to peace, security, and stability of Haiti, and in this context, underscores that individuals engaging in, directly or indirectly, or supporting criminal activities and violence involving armed groups and criminal networks that promote violence, or engaging in activities that destabilize Haiti through the illicit exploitation or trade of natural resources, may be listed for travel and financial measures;

Reaffirms its decision that Member States shall take appropriate steps to prevent the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and related materiel in Haiti, including through the strengthening of their border control mechanisms;

Calls upon Member States transferring firearms, ammunition, and related materiel to relevant Haitian authorities, either by sale or donation, to support those authorities in strengthening physical security, stockpile management, and post-delivery controls to mitigate the risk of diversion;

Encourages greater coordination among the Committee and its Panel of Experts, BINUH, UNODC, GSF, UNSOH, and other regional frameworks, on monitoring and facilitating the implementation of the sanctions regime, including the arms embargo, and on support to the Haitian authorities to strengthen the capacity of the HNP and FAd’H, and Haitian border and customs authorities to curb illicit arms flows, and further encourages the holding of regular briefings to the wider UN membership for information sharing and awareness raising;

Calls upon the Haitian authorities to strengthen the weapons and ammunition management capacity of the HNP and FAd’H, including through improved marking, recordkeeping, storage, and disposal of their national seized stockpiles of weapons and ammunition, and to reinforce border and customs controls, consistent with paragraph 1(e) of resolution 2793 (2025);

Confirms that, in line with paragraph 1(e) of resolution 2793 (2025), the GSF, should support the HNP and the Haitian armed forces to record and dispose of illicit arms, ammunition, and other materiel, seized as part of offensive operations or in the course of carrying out its mandate, as appropriate; and further calls upon the GSF to report any diversion of weapons and ammunition, including through loss and theft, to the Panel of Experts established pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022);

paragraph.subheading: Sanctions Committee and Panel of Experts

content.p: Decides that the mandate of the Committee, as set out in paragraph 19 of resolution 2653 (2022), shall apply with respect to the measures imposed in this resolution;

Decides to extend for a period of 13 months from the date of adoption of this resolution the mandate of the Panel of Experts, as specified in paragraph 21 of resolution 2653 (2022), and further decides that this mandate shall also apply with respect to the measures imposed in this resolution;

Directs the Committee to consider expeditiously the update of the list of individuals and entities designated pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022), taking into account the reports submitted by the Panel of Experts, including adding to the list individuals and entities that act in violation of the arms embargo imposed in this resolution;

Requests that the Panel of Experts provide to the Security Council, after discussion with the Committee, an interim report by 28 March 2027, a final report no later than 1 September 2027, and periodic updates in between, and reaffirms the Panel’s mandate to gather, examine, and analyze information regarding the implementation of the measures decided in this resolution;

Requests all Member States to regularly and in a timely manner inform the Panel of Experts and the Committee the concrete actions they have taken to fully implement this resolution, in order to facilitate the reporting work of the Panel of Experts and the sharing of best practices, requests the Panel of Experts to report on the implementation and effectiveness of this resolution in its regular reporting to the Security Council and further requests all parties, Member States, as well as international, regional, and subregional organizations, BINUH, UNSOH, and GSF to cooperate and share appropriate information with the Panel of Experts, including by facilitating the Panel of Experts’ access to persons, documents, and sites in a secure manner in order for the Panel to execute its mandate;

intro.p: Affirms that it shall keep the situation in Haiti under continuous review and that it shall be prepared to review the appropriateness of the measures contained in this resolution, including the strengthening, modification, suspension or lifting of the measures, as may be needed at any time in light of progress achieved on the following key benchmarks:

content.p: When the Haitian authorities have developed adequate judicial and rule of law capacity to address armed groups and criminal-related activities;

Progressive reduction in the amount of violence committed by armed groups and criminal networks, including the number of intentional homicides, kidnappings and incidents of sexual violence, as measured on an annual basis, beginning over the initial period of twelve months from adoption of this resolution;

Progressive decrease in the number of incidents of illicit trafficking and diversion of arms, as well as illicit financial flows therefrom, including by increasing the number and volume of arms seizures;

Requests in this regard the Secretary-General, in close coordination with the Panel of Experts, to conduct, no later than 1 September 2027, an assessment of progress achieved on the key benchmarks established in the paragraph above;

Requests the Haitian authorities to report, no later than twelve months from the date of adoption of this resolution and annually thereafter, to the Committee established pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022) concerning Haiti on the progress achieved on the key benchmarks in paragraph 16 of this resolution, and urges Haitian authorities to report and brief the UN Haiti sanctions committee annually on sanctions implementation progress, including legislative, regulatory, and enforcement actions as well as attendant challenges;
Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.
